title: Softening a Claim: Uyuni and Lithium

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *parece que*, *según parece*, *podría decirse que* and *tal vez convendría* from B2 Unit 21. A hedge keeps you from sounding more certain than you are. That matters with lithium, where plans change and many facts are still open.

sections.title: Four ways to soften
rows: Parece que el litio será importante para las baterías del futuro.
It seems that lithium will be important for the batteries of the future.
Según parece, los contratos de 2024 todavía necesitan la aprobación del Congreso.
Apparently the contracts of 2024 still need the approval of Congress.
Podría decirse que el litio es una oportunidad y también un reto.
One could say that lithium is an opportunity and also a challenge.
Tal vez convendría explicar mejor cómo se extrae el litio.
Perhaps it would be a good idea to explain better how lithium is extracted.

items.spanish: Parece que el Salar de Uyuni es lo que queda de antiguos lagos.
items.english: It seems that the Salar de Uyuni is what is left of ancient lakes.

items.spanish: Según parece, el gobierno quiere una nueva ley del litio.
items.english: Apparently the government wants a new lithium law.

items.spanish: Podría decirse que el salar es un lugar único.
items.english: One could say that the salt flat is a unique place.

sections.content: Use one hedge at a time. *Parece que* is followed by the indicative; *no parece que* takes the subjunctive: *No parece que sea fácil*. Hedges are for what you do not know; a number or a date from a source needs no hedge, only the source: *según el USGS*.
